paper.title_en: Ultraviolet emission from the $^{229\mathrm m}$Th isomer in neutron star mergers
paper.abstract_en: Thorium in the universe is primarily synthesized via the rapid neutron-capture process (r-process), with neutron star mergers serving as an important astrophysical site for its production. In particular, the heavy nucleus $^{229}$Th exhibits a unique low-energy isomeric state at 8.3 eV, giving rise to an isolated ultraviolet (UV) spectral line that has no analogue among known transitions in other heavy nuclei. In this work, we investigate the observational signatures associated with this low-lying state $^{229\mathrm m}$Th in neutron star mergers. For sufficiently neutron-rich trajectories, the FRDM2012 and WS4 nuclear mass models predict comparable $^{229}$Th abundances, with the isomer abundance reaches $\sim 10^{-6}$ for an assumed $^{229}$Ac $\beta $-decay feeding fraction of 14%. For the dynamical trajectory with a temperature of $\sim 10^{4}$ K, the effective transition rate from the low-lying state to the ground state is $\sim 10^{-4}$ s$^{-1}$, implying an effective lifetime on the order of hours. The decay transition of $^{229\mathrm m}$Th produces a distinct UV spectral feature near 1500 Å, providing a promising spectroscopic fingerprint for the direct and unambiguous identification of thorium in neutron star mergers. However, detecting UV lines remains a significant challenge with current instruments, particularly in the far-UV region at wavelengths below 2000 Å. Under the adopted ejecta and radiative transfer assumptions, the emission line would be detectable by the proposed Ultraviolet Explorer only from very nearby sources within $\mathcal {O}(10-100)~\textrm{kpc}$.
